uncited: This approach serves as a geometry confidence metric within the broader framework of [Geometry Confidence Measurement](15151-geometry-confidence-measurement.md), distinguishing true motion from depth estimation errors by leveraging the geometric constraint that static points must lie on their epipolar lines regardless of depth.
- Measured optical flow field $\mathbf{F}$ of shape $(H, W, 2)$, where $H$ and $W$ are height and width.
- Camera poses for source frame $i$ and target frame $j$: Rotation matrices $R_i, R_j \in \mathbb{R}^{3 \times 3}$ and translation vectors $C_i, C_j \in \mathbb{R}^3$.
- Camera intrinsics: focal lengths $f_x, f_y$ and principal point $(c_x, c_y)$.
- A confidence map (or residual map) $D \in \mathbb{R}^{H \times W}$ representing the point-to-line distance in pixels for each pixel.
- Pixel coordinate grids $X_s, Y_s \in \mathbb{R}^{H \times W}$ containing the x and y coordinates of each pixel in the source frame.
- Arbitrary depth values $z_l$ (near) and $z_f$ (far) used to construct the epipolar line.
**Construct Source Pixel Grids**: Create grids of pixel coordinates $(x_s, y_s)$ for the source frame $i$ with dimensions $H \times W$.
**Define Arbitrary Depths**: Select two arbitrary depth values, $z_l$ and $z_f$, to define the epipolar line.
**Reproject to Target Frame**: For each pixel $(x_s, y_s)$, convert to normalized camera coordinates and then to 3D points at depths $z_l$ and $z_f$ in frame $i$.
Transform these 3D points into frame $j$ using the relative pose $(R_j R_i^T, C_j - R_j R_i^T C_i)$.
Project these 3D points back to the image plane of frame $j$ using intrinsics to obtain two 2D points: $(u_1, v_1)$ corresponding to $z_l$ and $(u_2, v_2)$ corresponding to $z_f$.
**Compute Line Geometry**: Calculate the direction vector $\mathbf{d} = (u_2 - u_1, v_2 - v_1)$ and its norm $\|\mathbf{d}\|$.
**Compute Line Normal**: For valid pixels, compute the unit normal vector $\mathbf{n} = (n_x, n_y)$ to the epipolar line.
This is typically $(-d_y, d_x) / \|\mathbf{d}\|$ or $(d_y, -d_x) / \|\mathbf{d}\|$ depending on coordinate system orientation.
**Determine Correspondence**: Calculate the measured correspondence in frame $j$ by adding the measured flow to the original pixel coordinates: $(x_c, y_c) = (x_s + F_x, y_s + F_y)$.
**Compute Point-to-Line Distance**: Calculate the distance from the correspondence $(x_c, y_c)$ to the epipolar line defined by point $(u_1, v_1)$ and normal $\mathbf{n}$.
The distance is given by the absolute dot product: $D = |n_x(x_c - u_1) + n_y(y_c - v_1)|$.
Reshape the result to image dimensions $H \times W$.
- **Epipole Degeneracy**: If the pixel is near the epipole, the direction vector norm approaches zero.
- **Time Complexity**: $O(HW)$ per frame pair, as it involves per-pixel operations.
- **Memory Complexity**: $O(HW)$ for storing coordinate grids and intermediate projections.
- **When to Use**: When monocular depth estimates are unreliable or noisy, and camera poses are known.
- **When Not to Use**: When camera poses are unknown or highly inaccurate.
This method is part of the [Geometry Confidence Measurement](15151-geometry-confidence-measurement.md) pipeline, which aims to identify outliers in depth and flow consistency across views.
The approach exploits the property that static points lie on their epipolar lines regardless of their depth, allowing motion detection without depth priors.
